concept: Dynamic bucket sizing and cache-pressure closures

claims.text: When BucketCatalog memory exceeds timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold, the implementation archives or closes idle buckets. Archiving retains a small reopening record; if that is insufficient, archived entries are removed. Such memory-driven closure can still permit query-based reopening. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The minimum bucket-size floor can prevent further shrinking even when cardinality rises. Consequently, multiplying the allowed minimum by the active-bucket count can exceed the half-cache target; the target is not an enforced aggregate cache reservation. (medium confidence)

The large-measurement minimum-count exception does not universally prevent cache-derived closures. In the inspected code, a bucket below timeseriesBucketMinCount can still roll over for cache pressure when the incoming size exceeds the cache-derived absolute ceiling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The v8.0 serverStatus documentation distinguishes numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure, which records closures at the cache-derived dynamic size limit, from ordinary numBucketsClosedDueToSize closures. numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold and numBucketsArchivedDueToMemoryThreshold instead record bucket-catalog memory-budget reclamation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

SERVER-89233 records a sharded-cluster failure where newly inserted time-series data approached one bucket per document and reported cache-pressure closures. It lists affected versions 7.0.4 and 7.0.5 and fix versions 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0. A requested v7.0 backport is not evidence that a v7.0 fix shipped. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-25)

SERVER-82798 documents a bug in respecting the minimum time-series bucket size and lists fix versions 7.0.4 and 7.2.0-rc0. Its description connects an excessively small calculated limit with buckets containing few measurements. These are historical fix labels, not a guarantee against every later fragmentation bug. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-21)

Yannick Jaquier's MongoDB 8.0.5 NYC-taxi experiment reported 9,935,137 buckets with its original metadata configuration and 111,312 after removing metaField while retaining seconds granularity. This is independent evidence that schema choices can change bucket density, but the experiment provides no cache-pressure closure counters and cannot attribute the difference specifically to dynamic sizing. Its repeated metaField keys also limit interpretation of the original configuration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-08)

In the inspected master snapshot, getCacheDerivedBucketMaxSize computes storageCacheSizeBytes / (2 * workloadCardinality), clamps the derived limit to at least timeseriesBucketMinSize and at most INT_MAX, and caps the effective ordinary size limit at timeseriesBucketMaxSize. Zero cardinality returns the ordinary maximum. This describes the inspected development snapshot, not every released binary. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Inference for re-insertion remediation: rewriting the same measurements under unchanged global active-bucket cardinality and cache capacity can reproduce small buckets because the insertion path recomputes the dynamic limit. Increasing a bucket's time span alone does not remove this independent size limit. (medium confidence)

QuestDB's March 22, 2023 original benchmark used MongoDB Community 6.0.4. SERVER-105187 identifies dynamic sizing as introduced in 6.2. Therefore, that benchmark cannot directly validate the later dynamic-size mechanism or quantify the benefit of changing it; treating its ingestion figures as dynamic-sizing evidence would cross a version boundary. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-14)

SERVER-69899 introduced dynamic bucket sizing to avoid repeated disk writes when high-cardinality active buckets exceed WiredTiger cache capacity. Its design targets roughly half the cache for active buckets and accepts smaller buckets with worse space and query efficiency; that target is a policy objective rather than a guaranteed memory ceiling. (high confidence)

For a reinsertion experiment intended to improve bucket packing, compare closure-counter deltas and bucket counts under the intended concurrent workload, rather than relying only on a clean-start result. This is a methodological inference from the workload-sensitive report and the global sizing policy. (medium confidence)

A rising numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure counter alone does not establish that WiredTiger cache occupancy reached a measured pressure threshold. The inspected sizing calculation uses configured storage-cache size and active-bucket cardinality rather than a live occupancy measurement. Correlating cache and eviction telemetry is therefore necessary to establish actual storage-engine pressure. (medium confidence)

The dynamic sizing calculation combines active-bucket cardinality across collections. The cache-pressure closure counter therefore reflects a size heuristic based on cache capacity and bucket count; it does not by itself establish that measured cache occupancy or eviction pressure exceeded a threshold. (high confidence)

A 2023 interleaved multi-collection load report compared 25,000 buckets and 17 measurements per commit before competing load with 420,000 buckets, one measurement per commit, and 415,000 cache-pressure closures afterwards. These are workload-specific observations, not a general performance multiplier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-10-19)

SERVER-105187 says raising timeseriesBucketMinSize to timeseriesBucketMaxSize effectively disables dynamic shrinking. The same issue proposes making the calculation's constant configurable and remained unresolved in its July 14, 2025 record. This is an internal tuning lead requiring release-specific validation, not a generally safe remedy. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-14)

OneUptime independently describes high metaField cardinality as producing more buckets with fewer measurements and poorer compression. This supports cardinality as a packing concern, but the article does not independently verify MongoDB's dynamic-cap calculation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-31)

Dynamic sizing uses tracked active buckets, including open and archived buckets, and the cardinality is global across collections. A collection's effective bucket size can therefore depend on activity outside that collection. (medium confidence)

MongoDB documents that fine-grained or frequently changing metadata creates more sparse buckets and reduces storage and query efficiency. The independent taxi workload illustrates this density sensitivity. Reducing unnecessary metadata distinctions is a relevant workload hypothesis before re-insertion, but removing metadata can also change query behavior and must be evaluated for the application's access patterns. (medium confidence)
